facts.fact: Raghu's men took Dhanu and Gauri from the huts at moonrise while Kunal and Ila were in the Eye, held Dhanu in the open water at the Drum's seam to force names from him, and he died the first night. Dhanu gave only the names of his ewes. A clerk of Raghu's wrote the ransom note at first light on Dhanu's tally-hide, and Raghu's men took the whistle off the body.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires Gauri to explain Dhanu's death, the missing walnut and the bait; details are the minimum to make it concrete.

facts.fact: The queen's letter tells Ila that Harish went to the Under-Cairn guided by Prince Udai of Neshar, that what is owed is written down there, and that the crown has never dared read it.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Ila tell Kunal everything in the letter; consistent with the ch 16 midpoint and 'Tell no one Neshar's part'.

facts.fact: Gauri has laid stones over Dhanu's body at the Drum fold and will stay at the lake huts until the thaw.
facts.why: needed to ground Gauri staying at the huts until the thaw.

facts.fact: Gauri brings a lamp, a skin of oil, bread and dry boots for Ila to the cleft.
facts.why: needed so the pair can go on in the cleft with light; ch 29 opens with the lamp guttering.
